_coordinates: x = feet east of the 1871 east line of Jefferson Street; y = feet north of the north building line of DeKoven Street; z = feet above lot grade. Sources: maps plan_coordinates.csv (Greeley-Carlson 1891 atlas plate 28, Cook County parcel 17-16-324-029, 1855 alley ordinance), Andreas 1885 vol. 2 pp. 708-717 (Dalton, Lee, McDermott, plat p. 717), Musham 1940 pp. 94-95 and plan p. 98, Abbott 1871 stereograph of the O'Leary cottage (CHM ICHi-02741), inquiry testimony as reported in the Chicago Tribune 25-26 Nov 1871.

street.source: Greeley-Carlson 1891 plate 28 ('60'); Musham 1940 plan ('60 feet wide'); Sanborn 1906 sheet 110

alley.source: 1855 ordinance and 1891 plate (15 ft); Andreas plat draws 16 ft; Sullivan said 'about twelve feet'

oleary_137.source: E 1/2 of Lot 12, Block 38 (McDermott affidavit, Tribune 20 Oct 1871); lot lines from 1891 plate + parcel vertices, +-1.5 ft

dalton_135.source: W 1/2 of Lot 11; 1891 house number 135 at this half-lot

sullivan_134_south.source: E 1/2 of Lot 18 south of DeKoven; 1891 number 134; Bales: Catherine Sullivan's 75-ft tract, house on its east half-lot, vacant middle half-lot (Andreas: vacant lot west of Sullivan's)

white_west_132_south.source: Bales 2002 pp. 113, 195-199: William White's 'west parcel', 25 ft; Sullivan sat 'by a fence at the head of White's house or head of his lot'

white_east_130_south.source: Bales: White's 'east parcel' = E 1/2 of Lot 19; 1869-70 directory 'White William, lab. r. 130 DeKoven'

oleary_cottages.source: Andreas p. 714 (two cottages, 36 ft N-S, front nearly on the building line); Musham 16 ft wide; stereograph: one storey, gable to the street, on posts; east passage 'a large passage ... enough to roll' (Mrs McLaughlin, transcript p. 238 via Bales p. 231), so the cottage stands 0-3.5 ft from the west line

dalton_house.source: Andreas p. 714: on the west line of the lot, front 2 ft south of the north end of the O'Leary cottages, 40 ft deep, 4 ft above ground on cedar posts, one storey; width not recorded
dalton_house.y0_rule: oleary_cottages.y1 minus U(1,3) (Andreas: front 2 ft south of the north line of O'Leary's cottages)

forbes_cottages_133.source: Andreas plat: '1 1/2 Story Cottage occupied by Walter Forbes (front), William Lee (middle), Morris Connovan (rear)'; footprint not drawn; Musham draws three cottages in a row

barn_133.source: Andreas plat: '2 Story Barn 20 x 25' at the alley end of 133

dalton_shed.source: Andreas p. 714: shed 12 x 20 at the rear of the lot on the west side

variants.source: Andreas plat 1885 (drawn 16 E-W by 20 N-S, 9-ft passage on the east)
Musham 1940 plan (20 E-W by 16 N-S, 5-ft passage)

oleary_barn.source: Sullivan: 16 x 20, 14 ft high; Musham: about 16 ft high, peaked roof; Rau: about 20 ft high; Board: 'two-story barn'; Andreas plat: '1 1/2 Story Barn'

dalton_west_fence_house_to_shed.source: Andreas p. 714: 'a fence, eight feet high, ran from his house to his shed'

oleary_dalton_front_fence.source: Musham 1940: 'high wooden fences separated the lots'; Bales p. 233: Mrs McLaughlin's testimony suggests another fence ran from the front of Dalton's house; existence and height not recorded

street_pickets.source: stereograph shows a picket fence in front of the O'Leary cottage

oleary_shed.source: Patrick O'Leary: 'in a shed outside were some coal and more wood'; Sullivan: 'the shed adjoining the barn'; position not recorded; placed in the east passage in 40% of samples

P1_white_west_fence_Bales.note: Bales's placement: against White's fence at the building line, in front of White's west parcel

P2_white_east_130.note: in front of White's east parcel (No. 130)

P3_own_house_134.note: Andreas 1885: 'sitting in front of his own house, nearly opposite'

P4_vacant_lot_136.note: the vacant half-lot west of Sullivan's house

P5_opposite_oleary.note: Board of Police report: 'on the sidewalk on the south side of DeKoven street, and nearly opposite Leary's premises'

P1b_white_west_midpoint_Bales.note: Bales Appendix B: distance measured from the midpoint of White's west parcel; seated against the fence at the building line
